memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses: "Take the Levites from among all the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean. To purify them, do this: Sprinkle the water of cleansing on them; then have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes. And so they will purify themselves." - Num 8:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the Levites could begin their service to God, they had to be cleansed. Water was sprinkled on them, they shaved and washed — outward acts that pictured an inward truth: those who serve a holy God must first be made clean.

This tells us something important. Service to God flows out of a cleansed life, not the other way around. We do not clean ourselves up by working hard for God; rather, God cleanses us, and out of that cleansing we serve. The order matters. First made clean, then set to work.

We can never make ourselves truly clean by our own efforts, of course. The washing here was a picture, pointing to a deeper cleansing that only God can give. All the outward washing in the world cannot cleanse a heart.

This is exactly what Jesus came to do. His blood cleanses us from all sin (1 John 1:7). Paul reminds believers, "you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Cor 6:11). What the water of the tabernacle only pictured, Christ accomplishes in reality.

If you feel unworthy to serve God because of your failures and sin, hear the good news: God cleanses those He calls. Come to Him through Christ, be washed, and then serve from a clean heart. You do not clean yourself up to come to God; you come to God, and He cleanses you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you try to earn cleansing by your service, or receive it from God?
- How does Christ's cleansing free you to serve?
- Do you feel too unworthy to serve? What does this passage say?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that Your blood cleanses me from all sin. Wash my heart, and let me serve You out of the cleansing that only You can give. Amen.
